rationale: Near-identical pair: two uint8 images differing by 1/255 at a single pixel (perceptually identical to a human). A buggy LPIPS that fails to normalize inputs from uint8 [0,255] to the network's [-1,1] domain (e.g., feeding raw uint8 to a network trained on float32 [-1,1]) returns a non-trivial score driven by the 100× scale mismatch. The correct LPIPS scores this pair < 0.01 (perceptually identical). The meta-test asserts LPIPS < 0.05 — well below any plausible different-pair score.
